sources: McKay, John G. More West Highland Tales. Vol. 2. Scottish Anthropological and Folklore Society. Edinburgh: Oliver and Boyd, 1969, 369-370.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Canach, also named catkin or clòimh-chat, is a motif of Scottish folklore. The white wool of the marsh-dwelling cattail was once taken for shape-shifted witches. People said these witches rode the winds to their concealed meetings. A similar tale applied to snowflakes, which could conceal witches on their journey. Catkin fibers, carriers of seeds for trees such as birch and poplar, could be wound into small white strings. These strings were reputed to ward off witchcraft and other evil.

okr.objective: Canach is a Scottish folkloric motif of cattail wool taken for witches.
